import React from "react"; import { Container, Typography, Box, Paper, Button, Grid, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableContainer, TableHead, TableRow, } from "@mui/material"; import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom"; import { ArrowBack, PlayCircleOutline, CheckCircle, Cancel, } from "@mui/icons-material"; import Navigation from "../../components/Navigation"; const TermVsWholeLifePage: React.FC = () => { const navigate = useNavigate(); const comparison = [ { aspect: "Coverage Duration", term: "Specific period (10, 20, 30 years)", whole: "Entire lifetime", }, { aspect: "Premium", term: "Lower, affordable", whole: "Higher, more expensive", }, { aspect: "Cash Value", term: "No cash value", whole: "Builds cash value over time", }, { aspect: "Purpose", term: "Pure life protection", whole: "Protection + Investment", }, { aspect: "Payout", term: "Death benefit only", whole: "Death benefit + Maturity benefit", }, { aspect: "Best For", term: "Income replacement, debts", whole: "Estate planning, wealth building", }, ]; return ( <> Term vs. Whole Life Insurance A comprehensive comparison of the two most popular types of life insurance to help you make the right choice. 📋 Term Life Insurance Term life insurance provides coverage for a specific period. If you pass away during the term, your beneficiaries receive the death benefit. If you outlive the term, coverage ends with no payout. Key Features:
  • Most affordable option
  • Simple and straightforward
  • High coverage at low cost
  • Renewable or convertible options
  • No cash value accumulation
    • 💰 Whole Life Insurance Whole life insurance (also called permanent insurance) provides lifetime coverage. It includes a savings component (cash value) that grows over time, which you can borrow against or withdraw. Key Features:
  • Lifetime coverage guarantee
  • Builds cash value (tax-deferred)
  • Fixed premiums
  • Can borrow against cash value
  • More expensive premiums
    • Side-by-Side Comparison Aspect Term Life Whole Life {comparison.map((row, index) => ( {row.aspect} {row.term} {row.whole} ))}
    Choose Term Life If:
  • You need affordable, high coverage
  • You want to cover specific debts (mortgage, education)
  • You're young and need family protection
  • You want simple, straightforward insurance
  • Your budget is limited
    • Choose Whole Life If:
  • You want lifelong coverage guaranteed
  • You need estate planning tools
  • You want to build tax-deferred savings
  • You have dependents with special needs
  • You can afford higher premiums
    • Common Misconceptions
  • Myth: "Term insurance is a waste if I don't die during the term."
    Reality: It's like car insurance - you hope you don't need it, but it provides critical protection when you do.
  • Myth: "Whole life is always better because it builds cash value."
    Reality: The cash value growth is slow initially and the higher premiums might prevent you from getting adequate coverage.
  • Myth: "I can only have one or the other."
    Reality: Many people combine both - term for high coverage needs and whole life for permanent protection.
    • 💡 Real Example Scenario: Raj, 30 years old, married with 2 kids, needs ₹1 crore coverage
  • Term Plan Option: ₹12,000/year for 30 years (Total: ₹3.6 lakhs)
    Provides ₹1 crore coverage until age 60
  • Whole Life Option: ₹65,000/year for lifetime (Total: ₹19.5 lakhs in 30 years)
    Provides ₹1 crore coverage for life + builds cash value of ~₹8-10 lakhs in 30 years
    • 🎯 Not Sure Which is Right for You? While this page focuses on life insurance, our platform specializes in health insurance. Get personalized recommendations based on your health needs and budget.     );}; export default TermVsWholeLifePage;
